articles.title: 'Big Bang' Fix Puts Voyager Across the 'One Light-Day' Mark
articles.description: Flashback to 1977. Jimmy Carter was U.S. president, Star Wars was a box office hit, and the two Voyager spacecraft departed on an historic Grand Tour of the solar system. Now, teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are working to keep the missions active, as they push the boundaries of interstellar space beyond the solar system.
articles.summary: The Voyager spacecraft has crossed the one light-day distance mark, continuing humanity's most distant journey of exploration. Nearly 50 years after launch, Voyager remains a testament to human ingenuity and enduring exploration.

articles.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
articles.description: NASA is asking the public to send their names to Titan for an ambitious mission that will see a flying craft explore the Saturn moon in 2034, if all goes according to plan.
articles.summary: NASA's Dragonfly mission invites the public to send their names to Saturn's moon Titan aboard an ambitious flying spacecraft designed to explore this fascinating world. This groundbreaking mission will search for signs of life and study Titan's complex chemistry.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have found evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay occurring approximately once in every 10 billion events, a breakthrough after 42 years of searching. This discovery advances our understanding of fundamental physics and the subatomic world.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers observe two different types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart, an unprecedented cosmic phenomenon since the Big Bang.

articles.title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
articles.description: NASA announced a suite of awards and mission updates on Saturday to expand the agency’s Moon Base exploration, science, and infrastructure capabilities. The investments will advance commercial robotic deliveries, a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE, launch and orbital transfer services, and surface infrastructure as the agency works with American industry to establish a sustained presence on […]
articles.summary: NASA awards contracts for Moon Base transportation, technology, and science projects to advance lunar exploration. These initiatives represent major progress toward sustained human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps
articles.description: NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation […]
articles.summary: NASA opens applications for the next generation of astronauts to join its corps. This recruitment drive will shape the future of human spaceflight and exploration.

articles.title: The ELT Can Probe Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies and Their Dark Matter Mysteries
articles.description: Ultra-Diffuse Galaxies are strange because they're as large as the Milky Way, but have far fewer stars. It's as if they're puffed up for some reason. Determining what's going on with them could help confirm the Lambda-CDM model. A new proposed instrument for the Extremely Large Telescope could give astronomers their best look yet at these strange galaxies.
articles.summary: The Extremely Large Telescope will help solve the mystery of ultra-diffuse galaxies and their dark matter composition. These strange cosmic structures challenge our understanding of galaxy formation.

articles.title: NASA's Twin Spacecraft Will Execute Powered Slingshot Maneuvers on Their Way to Mars
articles.description: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features a pair of identical spacecraft on their way to Mars. They launched outside of the normal launch window, so they'll perform powered slingshot maneuvers to boost their speed. Once there, they'll "fly" in formation and study how the solar wind interacts with what remains of Mars ancient magnetosphere.
articles.summary: NASA's ESCAPADE mission features twin spacecraft executing innovative powered slingshot maneuvers en route to Mars. This groundbreaking trajectory represents a major achievement in interplanetary navigation.

articles.title: A Mighty Wind Blew Away Gas and Made Early Galaxies Brighter
articles.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies about 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang. But these galaxies should have been far less common so soon after the Big Bang. Researchers may have figured this out: Powerful ultraviolet (Lyman-alpha) radiation produced by dense clusters of young stars acted like a leaf blower, driving light-blocking gas and dust out of the galaxy and thereby making the galaxies appear brighter.
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope observations reveal that stellar winds in the early universe cleared gas and enhanced galaxy brightness. This discovery provides new insights into the evolution of galaxies in the infant cosmos.

articles.title: Interstellar Visitor 3I/ATLAS Shows Water Ice Behaves the Same Across Alien Star Systems
articles.description: Targets of opportunity sometimes happen in astronomy, and we got a major one when the third interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, was discovered in July 2025. And it just so happens that in the intervening years between the last known interstellar visitor (2I/Borisov in 2019), we got a major upgrade in our observational capabilities with the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). A new paper from a team of researchers led by Dr. Silvia Protopapa of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center and the Southwest Research Institute, and published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, details JWST’s findings on the water ice content of this most recent visitor from beyond our solar system.
articles.summary: The interstellar visitor 3I/ATLAS demonstrates that water ice behaves consistently across different star systems, providing insights into the universal nature of icy bodies beyond our solar system.

articles.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
articles.description: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A cosmological model proposing a 26.7 billion-year-old universe without dark matter or dark energy has passed rigorous tests, offering an intriguing alternative framework for understanding cosmic structure.

articles.title: Untangling the patterns of the cosmic microwave background to better understand the early universe
articles.description: A figure in red trudges across a blanket of white. Snow squeaks under the scientist's feet, too dry to be slick or soft. Only a line of flags and a few large buildings—the scientist's destination—break up the landscape. The sun hovers on the horizon, never quite setting against a blue sky devoid of clouds.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Scientists are decoding patterns in the cosmic microwave background to unlock deeper understanding of the early universe's structure and evolution.

articles.title: Robot successfully builds space structure in first autonomous construction demo
articles.description: A robotic truss builder that was conceived, designed and built by Caltech researchers has successfully built a structure in space—without the help of astronauts—for the first time. The truss builder, part of DARPA's Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design (NOM4D) program, consists of an autonomous manipulator that picks up struts and joints held in nearby dispensers to repeatedly assemble identical sections, or bays, of a perimeter truss.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Caltech engineers have successfully demonstrated autonomous robotic construction in space with their truss-building robot, advancing the future of off-world infrastructure development.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
articles.description: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky. The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust. Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.
articles.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has discovered two previously unknown satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, with hundreds more potentially waiting to be revealed.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft is capturing detailed views of the asteroids involved in NASA's groundbreaking 2022 kinetic impact experiment, studying the mission's outcomes.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, even as engineers battle dwindling power and mysterious technical problems. A clever energy-saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission, while an unexplained 48-hour communications blackout recently gave NASA a scare. On November 18, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, making even the simplest round-trip communication take 48 hours.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic milestone of one light-day distance from Earth nearly 50 years after launch, continuing its extraordinary journey of discovery.

articles.title: A hidden star is plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, new evidence suggests
articles.description: Something mysterious is disturbing Betelgeuse, and astronomers believe they have identified the culprit: a hidden companion star called Siwarha. New radio observations reveal that the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified a hidden companion star plowing through the atmosphere of Betelgeuse, explaining mysterious disturbances in this famous red supergiant. This discovery provides new insights into stellar interactions and the behavior of massive stars.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.description: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On November 7, 1992, NASA launched Mars Global Surveyor, its first Mars mission in 20 years, which revolutionized our understanding of the Red Planet through unprecedented mapping capabilities. This landmark mission laid the groundwork for modern Mars exploration.

articles.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
articles.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a a Dec. 3, 2025 confirmation hearing. In October of 2026, Isaacman sat down with Space.com to discuss the future of the space agency.
articles.summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman discusses the agency's ambitious Artemis program and the new international moon race in an exclusive interview. Isaacman expresses confidence in NASA's ability to succeed in returning humans to the lunar surface.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
articles.description: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova later caleld the Tycho supernova with his bare eyes. Here's why it mattered.
articles.summary: On November 6, 1572, German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed the Tycho supernova with his naked eye, initially thought to be a new star. This historic observation advanced our understanding of stellar explosions and the cosmos.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists used the Large Hadron Collider to peer into the zeptoverse, exploring the minuscule realm where exotic particles may exist. This research pushes the boundaries of what we can observe and understand about the fundamental nature of matter.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two additional dim satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, including an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy. These discoveries expand our understanding of the Milky Way's satellite system and galactic structure.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Research using nanohertz gravitational-wave observations provides new constraints on supermassive binary black holes existing at cosmic dawn. This study reveals insights into the formation and behavior of the universe's most massive objects in its earliest epochs.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Discovered the 6th Dwarf Planet
articles.description: The other five are Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
articles.summary: Researchers may have discovered a sixth dwarf planet, adding to our understanding of our solar system's distant objects.

articles.title: Astronomy Picture of the Day - A Farewell to Swift
articles.description: Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory. After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia. The featured image is a mosaic…
articles.summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory concludes nearly 22 years of groundbreaking service observing cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Studie: Artemis-II-Start verursacht Störung in der oberen Atmosphäre
articles.description: Die historische Artemis-II-Mission der NASA hat im April 2026 nicht nur Astronauten um den Mond fliegen lassen, sondern auch gewaltige Löcher in die obere Erdatmosphäre gerissen. Forscher warnen nun, dass solche Ereignisse GPS-Signale stören können.(Weiter le…
articles.summary: The historic Artemis II mission in April 2026 successfully flew astronauts around the Moon while creating measurable atmospheric ionospheric effects.

articles.title: Le télescope spatial Swift de la Nasa s'est désintégré dans l'atmosphère après 22 ans de mission
articles.description: Le télescope spatial Swift de la NASA s'est désintégré dans l'atmosphère terrestre le mercredi 4 novembre 2026 à 13h39 (heure de Paris) au-dessus de l'Indonésie. Lancé en 2004 pour une mission initiale de deux ans, cet observatoire de 1 450 kg a succombé au f…
articles.summary: After 22 years of service, NASA's Swift space telescope concludes its mission with a controlled atmospheric re-entry.

articles.title: M30’s Sparkling Stars
articles.description: This NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image released Nov. 5, 2026, provides a lesson in galactic history. The sparkling collection of stars is named Messier 30 (M30) after the French astronomer, Charles Messier, who cataloged M30 and other diffuse objects that might be mistaken for comets in the early telescopes of Messier’s time. M30 lies about […]
articles.summary: A Hubble Space Telescope image of globular cluster M30 reveals its sparkling stars and tells the story of galactic history. The observation demonstrates the power of modern telescopes to unlock cosmic secrets.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 6 – A Farewell to Swift

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Farewell […]
articles.summary: APOD bids farewell to the Swift space telescope, which made groundbreaking contributions to high-energy astrophysics. The mission's legacy will continue to inspire future gamma-ray observations.

articles.title: Our Sun’s Undiscovered Stellar Nemesis Is Still Out There, Says Physicist
articles.description: The decades old idea that our solar system’s Oort Cloud is continually perturbed by a heretofore undetected low mass Red Dwarf star remains the best explanation for periodicities found in Earth’s impact record.  Or so says a well known physicist who has long championed this idea.
articles.summary: A physicist explores the compelling hypothesis that an undiscovered low-mass companion star may periodically perturb our solar system's Oort Cloud. This theoretical research opens new avenues for understanding our cosmic neighborhood.
